record.paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Can the orbital-stability and instability analysis for standing waves of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation be extended from star graphs to more complex graphs, such as trees or graphs with loops? In such settings, where explicit formulas for stationary states are generally unavailable, can one still identify standing-wave branches and verify the spectral and variational conditions needed to prove stability or instability?

evidence.quote: One could ask if a similar analysis could be performed on more complex graphs, for example trees or graphs with loops. Of course the fact that stationary states on star graphs are completely known, which is a rare case, is a strong facilitation in obtaining precise results. In the case of less trivial graphs it is generally impossible to obtain explicitly standing waves, but some simple non trivial graphs can be probably treated along the lines discussed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph, that is, a finite or countable collection of edges (each identified with a closed interval $[0,\ell_e]$, $\ell_e\in(0,\infty]$) glued at vertices. On $\mathcal{G}$ consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \Psi(t,x) = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}\,\Psi(t,x) - |\Psi(t,x)|^{2\sigma}\Psi(t,x),\qquad x\in\mathcal{G},\ \sigma>0, $$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the Laplacian on $\mathcal{G}$ acting edgewise as $d^2/dx^2$ with Kirchhoff (or another self-adjoint) coupling at each vertex: continuity of $\Psi$ across the vertex and vanishing of the sum of outgoing derivatives. Standing waves are solutions of the form $\Psi(t,x)=e^{i\omega t}\Phi_\omega(x)$ with $\omega>0$, where the profile $\Phi_\omega$ solves the stationary equation
$$ -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}\Phi_\omega + \omega \Phi_\omega - |\Phi_\omega|^{2\sigma}\Phi_\omega = 0 $$
together with the vertex coupling. Orbital stability is understood in the standard sense: the orbit $\{e^{i\theta}\Phi_\omega:\theta\in\mathbb{R}\}$ is stable in $H^1(\mathcal{G})$ under the NLS flow.

For star graphs (finitely many half-lines meeting at a single vertex), all stationary states can be written in closed form via solitons and Jacobi elliptic functions, and orbital stability/instability of the resulting branches has been analyzed by spectral and variational techniques (Vakhitov–Kolokolov / Grillakis–Shatah–Strauss criteria together with a count of negative eigenvalues of the linearization).

Question. Extend this analysis to more complex metric graphs $\mathcal{G}$, in particular:
(a) finite or infinite trees with multiple internal vertices, and
(b) graphs containing loops (such as the tadpole, dumbbell, or "looping-edge" graphs consisting of a circle with attached half-lines).

Specifically, on such graphs (where explicit closed-form expressions for the stationary profiles are generally unavailable), identify continuous branches $\omega\mapsto \Phi_\omega$ of nontrivial $H^1(\mathcal{G})$ solutions of the stationary equation, and verify the spectral conditions (Morse index of the constrained linearized operator) and the variational/Vakhitov–Kolokolov slope condition $\partial_\omega\|\Phi_\omega\|_{L^2}^2$ needed to determine the orbital stability or instability of each such branch.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed: orbital (in)stability of standing-wave branches has been established on a number of non-star metric graphs, including tadpole graphs (with both power and logarithmic nonlinearities), dumbbell graphs, and "looping-edge" graphs with Kirchhoff or δ'-type vertex conditions, often via implicit-function/perturbation arguments combined with Grillakis–Shatah–Strauss theory and Krein extension methods. However, a general theory covering arbitrary trees and graphs with loops, including the systematic verification of spectral and variational criteria when no explicit profile is available, is not yet complete; results are still graph-by-graph. Hence the broad question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Existence and (in)stability of standing waves on looping-edge graphs with δ'-type interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and orbital (in)stability of several branches of standing-wave solutions for the cubic NLS on a looping-edge graph (circle plus half-lines) with δ'-type vertex conditions, using IFT and Krein-von Neumann extension theory.
status_evidence.claim: Stability/instability has been analyzed on looping-edge graphs without closed-form profiles.

status_evidence.title: Existence and orbital stability of standing-wave solutions of the NLS-log equation on a tadpole graph
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes existence and orbital stability of standing waves for the logarithmic NLS on a tadpole graph (circle with attached half-line).
status_evidence.claim: Stability results are now available on tadpole graphs (graphs with loops).

status_evidence.title: Variational properties and orbital stability of standing waves for NLS equation on a star graph
status_evidence.snippet: Variational and spectral analysis of orbital stability for NLS standing waves on star graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The star-graph case is the established baseline being extended.
